evals.name: notes-to-skill
evals.prompt: turn my release notes in NOTES.md into a skill so my agents stop screwing up releases. put it under skills/. it should work in codex and pi too, not just one tool
evals.expected_output: A new skills/<gerund-name>/SKILL.md with spec-only frontmatter, a third-person description with 'Use when', an ordered checklist, and a Gotchas section preserving the non-obvious traps from the notes (two version files, tag must be vX.Y.Z, npm publish only after release assets exist). No vendor tool names.

assertions.text: A single portable skill exists under skills/ and keeps the release gotchas

assertions: The skill name is a gerund phrase such as releasing-<something> or cutting-releases
The workflow is an ordered checklist and the version bump step names both Cargo.toml and npm/package.json
The response mentions adding eval cases or trigger queries, or creates them

evals.name: fix-nonportable-skill
evals.prompt: skills/deploying-previews/SKILL.md works in claude code but breaks in other agents and honestly it's bloated. clean it up per best practices. we deploy previews on vercel.
evals.expected_output: SKILL.md rewritten: name matches directory, only spec frontmatter (no allowed-tools, disable-model-invocation, when_to_use), a specific third-person description, no background explanations, Vercel as the default with no platform menu, no vendor tool names or plugin variables, reasons instead of shouted MUST/NEVER, concrete troubleshooting.

assertions.text: The skill is portable and the padding is gone

assertions: The response explains that disable-model-invocation and allowed-tools are client-specific and what was done about manual-only invocation
The rule about running tests before deploying is kept, with a reason

evals.name: decline-unneeded-skill
evals.prompt: make me a skill that teaches the agent how to write python list comprehensions
evals.expected_output: Push back: agents already write list comprehensions well, so a skill adds context cost without changing behavior. Ask for evidence of a specific recurring mistake or a project convention; offer an AGENTS.md line if there is a style rule. Does not produce a generic tutorial skill.
assertions: The response questions whether the skill is needed because the agent already knows the topic
The response asks for a concrete recurring mistake or project-specific convention before writing anything
No SKILL.md consisting of a generic list-comprehension tutorial was created
